title: Dynamic layered circuit breakers with safe degradation and model fallbacks
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: implement a hierarchical circuit breaker system that operates at multiple scopes (region, dependency, model, tenant) with dynamic trip thresholds and safe fallback behavior. This ticket covers design, prototype, and initial rollout for runtime and routing layers. The system should: 1) avoid cascading failures during region-level incidents; 2) allow targeted blocking of noisy tenants or expensive models without taking down the whole runtime; 3) support dynamic trip thresholds based on rolling error rate, p95/p99 latency, and headroom of GPU queues; 4) perform safe fallbacks (model variant, reduced max tokens, best-effort cached/responses, or degraded API contract) rather than opaque errors; 5) integrate with Console for visibility and manual overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Hierarchical breakers implemented: region -> dependency (eg. embeddings-store) -> model -> tenant
Dynamic trip logic using EWMA or sliding-window with tunable sensitivity is plumbed into runtime and routing layers
When a breaker trips, the system executes one of: (a) route to compatible cheaper model variant, (b) serve cached prefix/KV response, (c) return structured degraded response indicating reason and ETA
Console shows breaker state, last trip reason, and counts (requests attempted, blocked, degraded responses) per scope
Canary rollout completed for 10% traffic in us-west with automated rollback on regression in quality metrics
Unit and integration tests for breaker state transitions, race conditions, and metrics emitted
Runbook and incident playbook updated with breaker tuning knobs and escalation path
tasks: Design spec: breaker state machine and threshold formulas (EWMA alpha, min window, min reqs)
Runtime: add instrumentation and local in-memory breaker caches with persistence to redis for cross-process sync
Router: consult hierarchical breaker decisions before scheduling; implement fast-path for cache+fallback
Console: new UI card + API for overrides and historical timeline
E2E tests in staging with fault injector to simulate slow/failed dependency
Create alerting: sustained tripped_count > X and increase in degraded_response_rate > Y
